{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01P5tUE4engZ9mfgBcZdG1pD","type":"tool_result","content":"total 32\ndrwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo   512 Oct 25 12:31 .\ndrwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo   512 Oct 25 12:07 ..\n-rwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo   272 Oct 25 12:29 .drydock-persistence.json\n-rwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo   282 Oct 25 12:28 .env.example\ndrwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo   512 Oct 25 12:33 .git\n-rwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo   149 Oct 25 12:28 .gitignore\ndrwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo   512 Oct 25 12:28 .pytest_cache\ndrwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo   512 Oct 25 12:27 .venv\ndrwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo   512 Oct 25 12:28 bin\ndrwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo   512 Oct 25 12:32 cli\ndrwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo   512 Oct 25 12:33 data\n-rwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo   674 Oct 25 12:29 ledger\ndrwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo   512 Oct 25 12:29 persistence\n-rwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo   394 Oct 25 12:31 pyproject.toml\n-rwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo 12946 Oct 25 12:29 schema-verification.json\n-rwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo   879 Oct 25 12:29 schema.sql\ndrwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo   512 Oct 25 12:27 sources\ndrwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo   512 Oct 25 12:32 tests\n-rwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo  4655 Oct 25 12:27 uv.lock\ntotal 21\ndrwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo  512 Oct 25 12:27 .\ndrwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo  512 Oct 25 12:31 ..\n-rwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo 8513 Oct 25 12:07 run.sh\n-rwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo   87 Oct 25 12:07 seed_accounts.csv\n-rwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo  159 Oct 25 12:07 seed_categories.csv\n-rwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo 5699 Oct 25 12:07 seed_transactions.csv\n-rwxrwxrwx 1 barlo barlo  562 Oct 25 12:07 seed_transactions_bad.csv\n#!/bin/sh\n# run.sh — LayersTesting grader. Do not filter, skip, or reinterpret.\n#\n# Exercises ./ledger against a fresh database and compares every command's exit code and standard\n# output with the known answer below. Standard error is never compared.\n#\n#   sh sources/run.sh                    from the application root (how `drydock uat` runs it)\n#   sh uat/LayersTesting/bin/run.sh APP  from anywhere, grading the application root APP\n#\n# Database: DATABASE_URL when the caller sets it (for example a PostgreSQL DSN), otherwise a\n# SQLite file in a fresh temporary directory. Every run starts with `ledger init`, so the grader\n# never depends on prior state. Exit 0 only when every check passes.\nset -u\n\nHERE=$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")\" && pwd)\nAPP=$(cd \"${1:-.}\" && pwd)\nif [ -f \"$HERE/seed_accounts.csv\" ]; then SEED=$HERE; else SEED=$(cd \"$HERE/../sources\" && pwd); fi\nLEDGER=\"$APP/ledger\"\nWORK=$(mktemp -d)\ntrap 'rm -rf \"$WORK\"' EXIT INT TERM\nDATABASE_URL=${DATABASE_URL:-$WORK/ledger.db}\nexport DATABASE_URL\n\nif [ ! -x \"$LEDGER\" ]; then\n    echo \"error: no executable ./ledger at the application root $APP.\" >&2\n    echo \"The deliverable is an executable named ledger at the application root.\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nPASSED=0\nFAILED=0\n\n# check <id> <expected exit> <ledger args...>  — expected standard output on stdin.\ncheck() {\n    id=$1\n    want_rc=$2\n    shift 2\n    cat > \"$WORK/want\"\n    (cd \"$APP\" && \"$LEDGER\" \"$@\") > \"$WORK/got\" 2> \"$WORK/err\"\n    rc=$?\n    if [ \"$rc\" -eq \"$want_rc\" ] && cmp -s \"$WORK/want\" \"$WORK/got\"; then\n        PASSED=$((PASSED + 1))\n        echo \"PASS $id: ledger $*\"\n    else\n        FAILED=$((FAILED + 1))\n        echo \"FAIL $id: ledger $*\"\n        echo \"  exit: expected $want_rc, got $rc\"\n        diff \"$WORK/want\" \"$WORK/got\" | sed 's/^/  /'\n        sed 's/^/  stderr: /' \"$WORK/err\"\n    fi\n}\n\n# ── A. Accepts ``-?DIGITS[.D[D]]`` only; zero is rejected.\"\"\"\n    match = _AMOUNT.fullmatch(text)\n    if match is None:\n        raise Rejected(f\"amount must look like 12.50 or -3: {text!r}\")\n    sign, whole, fraction = match.groups()\n    cents = int(whole) * 100 + int((fraction or \"\").ljust(2, \"0\"))\n    if cents == 0:\n        raise Rejected(\"amount must not be zero\")\n    return -cents if sign else cents\n\n\ndef format_amount(cents: int) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return ``cents`` with exactly two decimals, a leading minus when negative, and no separators.\"\"\"\n    sign = \"-\" if cents < 0 else \"\"\n    magnitude = abs(cents)\n    return f\"{sign}{magnitude // 100}.{magnitude % 100:02d}\"\n\n\ndef validate_code(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return ``text`` if it is 1 to 12 characters from ``A-Z`` and ``0-9``.\"\"\"\n    if _CODE.fullmatch(text) is None:\n        raise Rejected(f\"code must be 1 to 12 characters of A-Z or 0-9: {text!r}\")\n    return text\n\n\ndef validate_text(text: str, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return ``text`` if its length is within bounds and it holds no comma or line break.\"\"\"\n    if not min_len <= len(text) <= max_len:\n        raise Rejected(f\"text must be {min_len} to {max_len} characters: {text!r}\")\n    if any(mark in text for mark in _FORBIDDEN_TEXT):\n        raise Rejected(\"text must not contain a comma or line break\")\n    return text\n\n\ndef validate_name(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return an account name or category description: 1 to 40 characters.\"\"\"\n    return validate_text(text, 1, 40)\n\n\ndef validate_memo(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return a transaction memo: 0 to 60 characters.\"\"\"\n    return validate_text(text, 0, 60)\n\n\ndef validate_date(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return ``text`` if it is a real calendar date written as ``YYYY-MM-DD``.\"\"\"\n    match = _DATE.fullmatch(text)\n    if match is None:\n        raise Rejected(f\"date must look like 2026-04-01: {text!r}\")\n    year, month, day = (int(part) for part in match.groups())\n    try:\n        datetime.date(year, month, day)\n    except ValueError as exc:\n        raise Rejected(f\"not a real calendar date: {text!r}\") from exc\n    return text\n\n\ndef account_balance(db: Database, account: str) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the sum of an account's transaction amounts in cents; zero when it has none.\"\"\"\n    return sum(row.amount for row in db.transactions.list(account=account))\n\n\ndef balance_guard(db: Database, deltas: Mapping[str, int]) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Reject the change set if any account's balance after its delta would go below zero.\n\n    ``deltas`` maps account code to a net change in cents. Nothing is written.\n    \"\"\"\n    for account in sorted(deltas):\n        resulting = account_balance(db, account) + deltas[account]\n        if resulting < 0:\n            raise Rejected(\n                f\"account {account} would be {format_amount(resulting)}; balance may not go negative\"\n            )\n===== cli/errors.py\n\"\"\"Expected failures and their exit codes. Each subclass maps to exactly one code.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass LedgerError(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Base for an expected failure. ``code`` is the process exit status.\"\"\"\n\n    code = 1\n\n    def __init__(self, message: str) -> None:\n        super().__init__(message)\n        self.message = message\n\n\nclass OperationalError(LedgerError):\n    \"\"\"The store or a file could not be used: unreachable, missing tables, unreadable file.\"\"\"\n\n    code = 1\n\n\nclass UsageError(LedgerError):\n    \"\"\"Unknown command, unknown table or report, or a wrong argument count.\"\"\"\n\n    code = 2\n\n\nclass Rejected(LedgerError):\n    \"\"\"Invalid input, duplicate key, unknown reference, account in use, or a negative balance.\"\"\"\n\n    code = 3\n\n\nclass NotFound(LedgerError):\n    \"\"\"An absent account or transaction id.\"\"\"\n\n    code = 4\n===== cli/registry.py\n\"\"\"The command table. Command modules call ``register`` on import; nothing else edits it.\"\"\"\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nfrom cli.errors import UsageError\n\nHandler = Callable[[list[str]], list[list[str]] | None]\n\n_COMMANDS: dict[tuple[str, ...], tuple[Handler, tuple[int, int]]] = {}\n\n\ndef register(words: tuple[str, ...], handler: Handler, nargs: tuple[int, int]) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Add a command. ``words`` is its name, ``nargs`` is the (min, max) argument count after it.\"\"\"\n    if not words:\n        raise ValueError(\"a command needs at least one word\")\n    if words in _COMMANDS:\n        raise ValueError(f\"command already registered: {' '.join(words)}\")\n    low, high = nargs\n    if low < 0 or high < low:\n        raise ValueError(f\"invalid argument count {nargs!r} for {' '.join(words)}\")\n    _COMMANDS[tuple(words)] = (handler, (low, high))\n\n\ndef lookup(argv: list[str]) -> tuple[Handler, list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Return the handler for the longest registered word prefix of ``argv`` and its arguments.\"\"\"\n    for size in range(len(argv), 0, -1):\n        entry = _COMMANDS.get(tuple(argv[:size]))\n        if entry is not None:\n            handler, (low, high) = entry\n            args = argv[size:]\n            if not low <= len(args) <= high:\n                raise UsageError(f\"{' '.join(argv[:size])}: expects {_count(low, high)} argument(s)\")\n            return handler, args\n    if not argv:\n        raise UsageError(\"no command given\")\n    raise UsageError(f\"unknown command: {' '.join(argv)}\")\n\n\ndef _count(low: int, high: int) -> str:\n    return str(low) if low == high else f\"{low} to {high}\"\n===== cli/testing.py\n\"\"\"In-process test entry: runs a command and returns what it wrote, without spawning a process.\"\"\"\n\nimport contextlib\nimport io\n\nfrom cli import main\n\n\ndef cli_runner(*args: str) -> tuple[int, str, str]:\n    \"\"\"Return (exit_code, stdout, stderr) for one command run in this process.\"\"\"\n    out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()\n    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out), contextlib.redirect_stderr(err):\n        code = main(list(args))\n    return code, out.getvalue(), err.getvalue()\n===== persistence/__init__.py\n\"\"\"Persistence for this Target. Shipped engines plus the schema generated from DATABASE.md.\"\"\"\n\nfrom .db import Database, PersistenceError, UnknownOperation\nfrom .schema import SCHEMA, open_database\n\n__all__ = [\"Database\", \"PersistenceError\", \"SCHEMA\", \"UnknownOperation\", \"open_database\"]\n===== persistence/db.py\n\"\"\"Persistence access for a Drydock Target.\n\nThis file is shipped by Drydock and copied into the build unchanged. Do not edit it here: edit\n``DATABASE.md`` and rebuild. It is hardened and tested once, in Drydock's own suite, so every\nTarget inherits a persistence layer that has already passed rather than one re-derived from prose\non each build.\n\nThe application-facing surface is ``Database``. One attribute per declared table, one method per\ndeclared access pattern::\n\n    db = Database(dsn, SCHEMA)\n    ticket = db.tickets.get(id=7)\n    open_tickets = db.tickets.list(status=\"open\")\n\n``schema.py`` beside this file is generated from ``DATABASE.md`` and carries the tables, the\noperations, and the row types. It contains no SQL. Statements are constructed here, by the driver\nfor the engine in use, so a parameter placeholder never appears in generated code or in a caller.\n\nValues reach the database as bound parameters, never as formatted text. Identifiers cannot be\nbound in any engine, so they are taken only from the generated schema — which Drydock validated\nagainst ``^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`` before emitting it — and are quoted on the way out.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Mapping, Sequence\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, fields\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager, nullcontext\nimport threading\nfrom typing import Any\n\n__all__ = [\n    \"Database\",\n    \"Driver\",\n    \"Operation\",\n    \"PersistenceError\",\n    \"Schema\",\n    \"Table\",\n    \"statements\",\n    \"UnknownOperation\",\n    \"begin_acceptance_transaction\",\n    \"end_acceptance_transaction\",\n]\n\nVERBS = (\"get\", \"list\", \"create\", \"update\", \"delete\")\n#: The comparisons a declared Match term may state; anything else is refused before SQL is built.\nCOMPARISONS = (\"=\", \"<\", \"<=\", \">\", \">=\")\nDIRECTIONS = (\"asc\", \"desc\")\n\n\nclass PersistenceError(RuntimeError):\n    \"\"\"A persistence failure the caller may act on, raised in place of a driver exception.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass UnknownOperation(PersistenceError):\n    \"\"\"A verb was requested that the declaration does not grant for that table.\"\"\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Table:\n    \"\"\"One declared table: its columns and the column that identifies a row.\"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    columns: tuple[str, ...]\n    primary_key: str | None = None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Operation:\n    \"\"\"One declared access pattern, reduced to what executing it requires.\n\n    ``name`` is the method callers use and ``verb`` is its Kind, how it runs; a name that is a\n    verb runs as that verb. ``inputs`` are the parameters the caller supplies. ``match`` is the\n    equality predicate of a ``get``, ``update``, ``upsert``, or ``delete``, every field of it\n    required; a ``list`` filters on whichever inputs are supplied, and the inputs of a\n    ``create``, ``update``, or ``upsert`` outside ``match`` are the values written. ``row`` is the dataclass the operation returns, and\n    ``columns`` are its fields; an operation with no ``row`` returns a count. ``compare`` holds\n    ``(field, op, column)`` for each input compared other than by equality with its own column,\n    such as ``(\"start_date\", \">=\", \"date\")``, and ``order`` the ``(column, direction)`` sort keys\n    of a ``list``.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    identifier: str\n    table: str\n    verb: str\n    inputs: tuple[str, ...]\n    row: type | None = None\n    columns: tuple[str, ...] = ()\n    match: tuple[str, ...] = ()\n    name: str = \"\"\n    compare: tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...] = ()\n    order: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = ()\n\n    def keys(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:\n        \"\"\"The match fields compared by equality: what reads back the one row a write reached.\"\"\"\n        compared = {field for field, op, _ in self.compare if op != \"=\"}\n        return tuple(name for name in self.match if name not in compared)\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Schema:\n    \"\"\"The generated declaration: every table and every operation reaching one.\"\"\"\n\n    tables: tuple[Table, ...]\n    operations: tuple[Operation, ...]\n\n    def by_table(self) -> dict[str, tuple[Operation, ...]]:\n        grouped: dict[str, list[Operation]] = {table.name: [] for table in self.tables}\n        for operation in self.operations:\n            grouped.setdefault(operation.table, []).append(operation)\n        return {name: tuple(items) for name, items in grouped.items()}\n\n\nclass Driver:\n    \"\"\"Statement construction shared by every engine.\n\n    Subclasses supply connection handling and the two things engines genuinely disagree about:\n    how a parameter is spelled, and how a freshly inserted row reports its key. Everything else is\n    identical SQL, so it is written once here rather than twice in the engines.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def prepare_schema(self, sql: str) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Translate generated DDL for this engine.\"\"\"\n        return sql\n\n    #: Spelled by the DB-API driver, not by this class's callers.\n    paramstyle = \"qmark\"\n    returning = False\n\n    def connect(self) -> Any:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def pin(self) -> Any:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        \"\"\"Serve one connection to every thread until ``close``. The acceptance harness's.\"\"\"\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def identity(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        \"\"\"Name the store, so two spellings of one DSN share one acceptance transaction.\"\"\"\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def close(self) -> None:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def placeholder(self, index: int) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Render parameter ``index`` (0-based) in this engine's spelling.\"\"\"\n        return \"?\" if self.paramstyle == \"qmark\" else \"%s\"\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def quote(identifier: str) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Quote a declared identifier. Never called with caller-supplied text.\"\"\"\n        if not identifier.replace(\"_\", \"\").isalnum():\n            raise PersistenceError(f\"refusing unsafe identifier {identifier!r}\")\n        return f'\"{identifier}\"'\n\n    def _predicate(\n        self, names: Sequence[str], start: int = 0, compare: Sequence[tuple[str, str, str]] = ()\n    ) -> str:\n        \"\"\"``names`` are input fields; each is compared with its declared column, else its own.\"\"\"\n        by_field = {field: (op, column) for field, op, column in compare}\n        terms = []\n        for offset, name in enumerate(names):\n            op, column = by_field.get(name, (\"=\", name))\n            if op not in COMPARISONS:\n                raise PersistenceError(f\"refusing undeclared comparison {op!r}\")\n            terms.append(f\"{self.quote(column)} {op} {self.placeholder(start + offset)}\")\n        return \" AND \".join(terms)\n\n    def select(\n        self,\n        table: str,\n        columns: Sequence[str],\n        predicate: Sequence[str],\n        compare: Sequence[tuple[str, str, str]] = (),\n        order: Sequence[tuple[str, str]] = (),\n    ) -> str:\n        selected = \".join(self.quote(name) for name in columns)\n        marks = \", \".join(self.placeholder(index) for index in range(len(columns)))\n        statement = f\"INSERT INTO {self.quote(table)} ({names})     columns: Sequence[str],\n        predicate: Sequence[str],\n        compare: Sequence[tuple[str, str, str]] = (),\n    ) -> str:\n        assignments = \", \".join(\n            f\"{self.quote(name)} = {self.placeholder(index)}\" for index, name in enumerate(columns)\n        )\n        statement = f\"UPDATE {self.quote(table)} SET {assignments}\"\n        if predicate:\n            statement += f\" WHERE {self._predicate(predicate, len(columns), compare)}\"\n        return statement\n\n    def upsert(self, table: str, columns: Sequence[str], match: Sequence[str]) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Insert a row, or replace the Set columns of the row ``match`` identifies.\n\n        ``match`` names a declared unique key, which is what ``ON CONFLICT`` requires; SQLite\n        and PostgreSQL spell the statement identically.\n        \"\"\"\n        assigned = [name for name in columns if name not in match]\n        target = \", \".join(self.quote(name) for name in match)\n        action = (\n            \"DO UPDATE SET \"\n            + \", \".join(f\"{self.quote(name)} = excluded.{self.quote(name)}\" for name in assigned)\n            if assigned\n            else \"DO NOTHING\"\n        )\n        return f\"{self.insert(table, columns, None)} ON CONFLICT ({target}) {action}\"\n\n    def delete(\n        self, table: str, predicate: Sequence[str], compare: Sequence[tuple[str, str, str]] = ()\n    ) -> str:\n        statement = f\"DELETE FROM {self.quote(table)}\"\n        if predicate:\n            statement += f\" WHERE {self._predicate(predicate, 0, methods one table grants, bound from the declaration rather than defined by hand.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, table: Table, operations: Iterable[Operation], database: Database) -> None:\n        self._table = table\n        self._database = database\n        self._operations = {operation.name or operation.verb: operation for operation in operations}\n\n    def __repr__(self) -> str:\n        granted = \", \".join(sorted(self._operations))\n        return f\"<TableAccess {self._table.name}: {granted or 'no declared operation'}>\"\n\n    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> Callable[..., Declared: {granted}. \"\n                \"Add an access pattern to DATABASE.md rather than reaching around this class.\"\n            )\n        return lambda **arguments: self._database.run(operation, arguments)\n\n\nclass _AcceptanceTransaction:\n    \"\"\"One transaction per store, shared by every ``Database`` this process opens; never committed.\n\n    The acceptance harness begins it before a criterion runs and rolls it back when the criterion\n    ends. A crash loses nothing: an engine discards an uncommitted transaction.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self) -> None:\n        self.lock = threading.RLock()\n        self._drivers: dict[str, Driver] = {}\n\n    def join(self, driver: Driver) -> Driver:\n        with self.lock:\n            shared = self._drivers.get(driver.identity())\n            if shared is None:\n                cursor = driver.pin().cursor()\n                try:\n                    cursor.execute(\"BEGIN\")\n                finally:\n                    cursor.close()\n                shared = self._drivers[driver.identity()] = driver\n            return shared\n\n    def rollback(self) -> None:\n        failures = []\n        with self.lock:\n            for identity, driver in self._drivers.items():\n                try:\n                    cursor = driver.pin().cursor()\n                    try:\n                        cursor.execute(\"ROLLBACK\")\n                    finally:\n                        cursor.close()\n                except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - every store is still closed\n                    failures.append(f\"{identity}: {exc}\")\n                finally:\n                    driver.close()\n            self._drivers.clear()\n        if failures:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"acceptance rollback failed: \" + \"; translated at the boundary on purpose\n            raise PersistenceError(f\"{action} could not connect: {exc}\") from exc\n\n    def _dispatch(\n        self,\n        operation: Operation,\n        cursor: Any,\n        names: list[str],\n        values: list[Any],\n    ) -> Any:\n        verb = operation.verb\n        table = operation.table\n        match = self._match(operation)\n        if verb in (\"get\", \"list\"):\n            columns = operation.columns or self._columns(table)\n            statement = self._driver.select(\n                table, columns, names, operation.compare, operation.order\n            )\n            cursor.execute(statement, values)\n            rows = cursor.fetchall() if verb == \"list\" else cursor.fetchmany(1)\n            built = [self._build(operation, columns, row) for row in rows]\n            return built if verb == \"","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false,"persistedOutputPath":"/home/barlo/.drydock/claude-home/projects/-mnt-c-Users-barlo-projects-drydock-uat-LayersTesting-runs-20261025-160726-build-LayersTesting/3078c6c5-245a-4f57-9bc2-b3265db7f953/tool-results/bl81t0j7j.txt","persistedOutputSize":51039},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01UVrGEYPAFwuUx8vw6eF2ER","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01QdYnWcdDH5bTNr3rJVCf6S","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"Database location: DATABASE_URL, then DATABASE_PATH, then data/app.db under the application root.\"\"\"\n\nfrom collections.abc import Mapping\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nAPP_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent\nDEFAULT_DATABASE_PATH = APP_ROOT / \"data\" / \"app.db\"\n\n\ndef resolve_dsn(environ: Mapping[str, str]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return the configured store location as written. An empty value counts as unset.\"\"\"\n    return (\n        environ.get(\"DATABASE_URL\")\n        or environ.get(\"DATABASE_PATH\")\n        or str(DEFAULT_DATABASE_PATH)\n    )\n\"\"\"Opens the declared store for a command. The only caller of ``persistence.open_database``.\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom persistence import Database, open_database\n\nfrom cli.config import resolve_dsn\n\nSQLITE_PREFIX = \"sqlite://\"\n\n\ndef open_store() -> Database:\n    \"\"\"Open the store named by the environment, creating a missing SQLite parent directory first.\"\"\"\n    dsn = resolve_dsn(os.environ)\n    path = _sqlite_path(dsn)\n    if path is not None:\n        Path(path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    return open_database(dsn)\n\n\ndef _sqlite_path(dsn: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the file path a SQLite DSN names, or None for any other engine.\"\"\"\n    if dsn.startswith(SQLITE_PREFIX):\n        return dsn[len(SQLITE_PREFIX):]\n    if \"://\" not in dsn:\n        return dsn\n    return None\n\"\"\"Expected failures and their exit codes. Each subclass maps to exactly one code.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass LedgerError(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Base for an expected failure. ``code`` is the process exit status.\"\"\"\n\n    code = 1\n\n    def __init__(self, message: str) -> None:\n        super().__init__(message)\n        self.message = message\n\n\nclass OperationalError(LedgerError):\n    \"\"\"The store or a file could not be used: unreachable, missing tables, unreadable file.\"\"\"\n\n    code = 1\n\n\nclass UsageError(LedgerError):\n    \"\"\"Unknown command, unknown table or report, or a wrong argument count.\"\"\"\n\n    code = 2\n\n\nclass Rejected(LedgerError):\n    \"\"\"Invalid input, duplicate key, unknown reference, account in use, or a negative balance.\"\"\"\n\n    code = 3\n\n\nclass NotFound(LedgerError):\n    \"\"\"An absent account or transaction id.\"\"\"\n\n    code = 4\n\"\"\"The command table. Command modules call ``register`` on import; nothing else edits it.\"\"\"\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nfrom cli.errors import UsageError\n\nHandler = Callable[[list[str]], list[list[str]] | None]\n\n_COMMANDS: dict[tuple[str, ...], tuple[Handler, tuple[int, int]]] = {}\n\n\ndef register(words: tuple[str, ...], handler: Handler, nargs: tuple[int, int]) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Add a command. ``words`` is its name, ``nargs`` is the (min, max) argument count after it.\"\"\"\n    if not words:\n        raise ValueError(\"a command needs at least one word\")\n    if words in _COMMANDS:\n        raise ValueError(f\"command already registered: {' '.join(words)}\")\n    low, high = nargs\n    if low < 0 or high < low:\n        raise ValueError(f\"invalid argument count {nargs!r} for {' '.join(words)}\")\n    _COMMANDS[tuple(words)] = (handler, (low, high))\n\n\ndef lookup(argv: list[str]) -> tuple[Handler, list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Return the handler for the longest registered word prefix of ``argv`` and its arguments.\"\"\"\n    for size in range(len(argv), 0, -1):\n        entry = _COMMANDS.get(tuple(argv[:size]))\n        if entry is not None:\n            handler, (low, high) = entry\n            args = argv[size:]\n            if not low <= len(args) <= high:\n                raise UsageError(f\"{' '.join(argv[:size])}: expects {_count(low, high)} argument(s)\")\n            return handler, args\n    if not argv:\n        raise UsageError(\"no command given\")\n    raise UsageError(f\"unknown command: {' '.join(argv)}\")\n\n\ndef _count(low: int, high: int) -> str:\n    return str(low) if low == high else f\"{low} to {high}\"\n\"\"\"In-process test entry: runs a command and returns what it wrote, without spawning a process.\"\"\"\n\nimport contextlib\nimport io\n\nfrom cli import main\n\n\ndef cli_runner(*args: str) -> tuple[int, str, str]:\n    \"\"\"Return (exit_code, stdout, stderr) for one command run in this process.\"\"\"\n    out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()\n    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out), contextlib.redirect_stderr(err):\n        code = main(list(args))\n    return code, out.getvalue(), {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01XCGFfoJrCYuL9UG6r3qq9A","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"Persistence for this Target. Shipped engines plus the schema generated from DATABASE.md.\"\"\"\n\nfrom .db import Database, PersistenceError, UnknownOperation\nfrom .schema import SCHEMA, open_database\n\n__all__ = [\"Database\", \"PersistenceError\", \"SCHEMA\", \"UnknownOperation\", \"open_database\"]\n\"\"\"Persistence access for a Drydock Target.\n\nThis file is shipped by Drydock and copied into the build unchanged. Do not edit it here: edit\n``DATABASE.md`` and rebuild. It is hardened and tested once, in Drydock's own suite, so every\nTarget inherits a persistence layer that has already passed rather than one re-derived from prose\non each build.\n\nThe application-facing surface is ``Database``. One attribute per declared table, one method per\ndeclared access pattern::\n\n    db = Database(dsn, SCHEMA)\n    ticket = db.tickets.get(id=7)\n    open_tickets = db.tickets.list(status=\"open\")\n\n``schema.py`` beside this file is generated from ``DATABASE.md`` and carries the tables, the\noperations, and the row types. It contains no SQL. Statements are constructed here, by the driver\nfor the engine in use, so a parameter placeholder never appears in generated code or in a caller.\n\nValues reach the database as bound parameters, never as formatted text. Identifiers cannot be\nbound in any engine, so they are taken only from the generated schema — which Drydock validated\nagainst ``^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`` before emitting it — and are quoted on the way out.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Mapping, Sequence\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, fields\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager, nullcontext\nimport threading\nfrom typing import Any\n\n__all__ = [\n    \"Database\",\n    \"Driver\",\n    \"Operation\",\n    \"PersistenceError\",\n    \"Schema\",\n    \"Table\",\n    \"statements\",\n    \"UnknownOperation\",\n    \"begin_acceptance_transaction\",\n    \"end_acceptance_transaction\",\n]\n\nVERBS = (\"get\", \"list\", \"create\", \"update\", \"delete\")\n#: The comparisons a declared Match term may state; anything else is refused before SQL is built.\nCOMPARISONS = (\"=\", \"<\", \"<=\", \">\", \">=\")\nDIRECTIONS = (\"asc\", \"desc\")\n\n\nclass PersistenceError(RuntimeError):\n    \"\"\"A persistence failure the caller may act on, raised in place of a driver exception.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass UnknownOperation(PersistenceError):\n    \"\"\"A verb was requested that the declaration does not grant for that table.\"\"\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Table:\n    \"\"\"One declared table: its columns and the column that identifies a row.\"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    columns: tuple[str, ...]\n    primary_key: str | None = None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Operation:\n    \"\"\"One declared access pattern, reduced to what executing it requires.\n\n    ``name`` is the method callers use and ``verb`` is its Kind, how it runs; a name that is a\n    verb runs as that verb. ``inputs`` are the parameters the caller supplies. ``match`` is the\n    equality predicate of a ``get``, ``update``, ``upsert``, or ``delete``, every field of it\n    required; a ``list`` filters on whichever inputs are supplied, and the inputs of a\n    ``create``, ``update``, or ``upsert`` outside ``match`` are the values written. ``row`` is the dataclass the operation returns, and\n    ``columns`` are its fields; an operation with no ``row`` returns a count. ``compare`` holds\n    ``(field, op, column)`` for each input compared other than by equality with its own column,\n    such as ``(\"start_date\", \">=\", \"date\")``, and ``order`` the ``(column, direction)`` sort keys\n    of a ``list``.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    identifier: str\n    table: str\n    verb: str\n    inputs: tuple[str, ...]\n    row: type | None = None\n    columns: tuple[str, ...] = ()\n    match: tuple[str, ...] = ()\n    name: str = \"\"\n    compare: tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...] = ()\n    order: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = ()\n\n    def keys(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:\n        \"\"\"The match fields compared by equality: what reads back the one row a write reached.\"\"\"\n        compared = {field for field, op, _ in self.compare if op != \"=\"}\n        return tuple(name for name in self.match if name not in compared)\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Schema:\n    \"\"\"The generated declaration: every table and every operation reaching one.\"\"\"\n\n    tables: tuple[Table, ...]\n    operations: tuple[Operation, ...]\n\n    def by_table(self) -> dict[str, tuple[Operation, ...]]:\n        grouped: dict[str, list[Operation]] = {table.name: [] for table in self.tables}\n        for operation in self.operations:\n            grouped.setdefault(operation.table, []).append(operation)\n        return {name: tuple(items) for name, items in grouped.items()}\n\n\nclass Driver:\n    \"\"\"Statement construction shared by every engine.\n\n    Subclasses supply connection handling and the two things engines genuinely disagree about:\n    how a parameter is spelled, and how a freshly inserted row reports its key. Everything else is\n    identical SQL, so it is written once here rather than twice in the engines.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def prepare_schema(self, sql: str) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Translate generated DDL for this engine.\"\"\"\n        return sql\n\n    #: Spelled by the DB-API driver, not by this class's callers.\n    paramstyle = \"qmark\"\n    returning = False\n\n    def connect(self) -> Any:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def pin(self) -> Any:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        \"\"\"Serve one connection to every thread until ``close``. The acceptance harness's.\"\"\"\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def identity(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        \"\"\"Name the store, so two spellings of one DSN share one acceptance transaction.\"\"\"\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def close(self) -> None:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def placeholder(self, index: int) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Render parameter ``index`` (0-based) in this engine's spelling.\"\"\"\n        return \"?\" if self.paramstyle == \"qmark\" else \"%s\"\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def quote(identifier: str) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Quote a declared identifier. Never called with caller-supplied text.\"\"\"\n        if not identifier.replace(\"_\", \"\").isalnum():\n            raise PersistenceError(f\"refusing unsafe identifier {identifier!r}\")\n        return f'\"{identifier}\"'\n\n    def _predicate(\n        self, names: Sequence[str], start: int = 0, compare: Sequence[tuple[str, str, str]] = ()\n    ) -> str:\n        \"\"\"``names`` are input fields; each is compared with its declared column, else its own.\"\"\"\n        by_field = {field: (op, column) for field, op, column in compare}\n        terms = []\n        for offset, name in enumerate(names):\n            op, column = by_field.get(name, (\"=\", name))\n            if op not in COMPARISONS:\n                raise PersistenceError(f\"refusing undeclared comparison {op!r}\")\n            terms.append(f\"{self.quote(column)} {op} {self.placeholder(start + offset)}\")\n        return \" AND \".join(terms)\n\n    def select(\n        self,\n        table: str,\n        columns: Sequence[str],\n        predicate: Sequence[str],\n        compare: Sequence[tuple[str, str, str]] = (),\n        order: Sequence[tuple[str, str]] = (),\n    ) -> str:\n        selected = \", \".join(self.quote(name) for name in columns)\n        statement = f\"SELECT {selected} FROM {self.quote(table)}\"\n        if predicate:\n            statement += f\" WHERE {self._predicate(predicate, 0, compare)}\"\n        if order:\n            for _, direction in order:\n                if direction not in DIRECTIONS:\n                    raise PersistenceError(f\"refusing undeclared order {direction!r}\")\n            keys = \", \".join(\n                f\"{self.quote(column)} {direction.upper()}\" for column, direction in order\n            )\n            statement += f\" ORDER BY {keys}\"\n        return statement\n\n    def insert(self, table: str, columns: Sequence[str], key: str | None) -> str:\n        names = \", \".join(self.quote(name) for name in columns)\n        marks = \", \".join(self.placeholder(index) for index in range(len(columns)))\n        statement = f\"INSERT INTO {self.quote(table)} ({names}) VALUES ({marks})\"\n        if self.returning and key:\n            statement += f\" RETURNING {self.quote(key)}\"\n        return statement\n\n    def update(\n        self,\n        table: str,\n        columns: Sequence[str],\n        predicate: Sequence[str],\n        compare: Sequence[tuple[str, str, str]] = (),\n    ) -> str:\n        assignments = \", \".join(\n            f\"{self.quote(name)} = {self.placeholder(index)}\" for index, name in enumerate(columns)\n        )\n        statement = f\"UPDATE {self.quote(table)} SET {assignments}\"\n        if predicate:\n            statement += f\" WHERE {self._predicate(predicate, len(columns), compare)}\"\n        return statement\n\n    def upsert(self, table: str, columns: Sequence[str], match: Sequence[str]) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Insert a row, or replace the Set columns of the row ``match`` identifies.\n\n        ``match`` names a declared unique key, which is what ``ON CONFLICT`` requires; SQLite\n        and PostgreSQL spell the statement identically.\n        \"\"\"\n        assigned = [name for name in columns if name not in match]\n        target = \", \".join(self.quote(name) for name in match)\n        action = (\n            \"DO UPDATE SET \"\n            + \", \".join(f\"{self.quote(name)} = excluded.{self.quote(name)}\" for name in assigned)\n            if assigned\n            else \"DO NOTHING\"\n        )\n        return f\"{self.insert(table, columns, None)} ON CONFLICT ({target}) {action}\"\n\n    def delete(\n        self, table: str, predicate: Sequence[str], compare: Sequence[tuple[str, str, str]] = ()\n    ) -> str:\n        statement = f\"DELETE FROM {self.quote(table)}\"\n        if predicate:\n            statement += f\" WHERE {self._predicate(predicate, 0, compare)}\"\n        return statement\n\n    def inserted_key(self, cursor: Any) -> Any:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n\nclass TableAccess:\n    \"\"\"The methods one table grants, bound from the declaration rather than defined by hand.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, table: Table, operations: Iterable[Operation], database: Database) -> None:\n        self._table = table\n        self._database = database\n        self._operations = {operation.name or operation.verb: operation for operation in operations}\n\n    def __repr__(self) -> str:\n        granted = \", \".join(sorted(self._operations))\n        return f\"<TableAccess {self._table.name}: {granted or 'no declared operation'}>\"\n\n    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> Callable[..., Any]:\n        operation = self._operations.get(name)\n        if operation is None:\n            granted = \", \".join(sorted(self._operations)) or \"none\"\n            raise UnknownOperation(\n                f\"{self._table.name} declares no {name!r} operation. Declared: {granted}. \"\n                \"Add an access pattern to DATABASE.md rather than reaching around this class.\"\n            )\n        return lambda **arguments: self._database.run(operation, arguments)\n\n\nclass _AcceptanceTransaction:\n    \"\"\"One transaction per store, shared by every ``Database`` this process opens; never committed.\n\n    The acceptance harness begins it before a criterion runs and rolls it back when the criterion\n    ends. The criterion's fixture, the application behind an in-process HTTP client, and an\n    in-process command all join it, so setup, behavior and readback see one another's writes and\n    none of them persists. A crash loses nothing: an engine discards an uncommitted transaction.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self) -> None:\n        self.lock = threading.RLock()\n        self._drivers: dict[str, Driver] = {}\n\n    def join(self, driver: Driver) -> Driver:\n        with self.lock:\n            shared = self._drivers.get(driver.identity())\n            if shared is None:\n                cursor = driver.pin().cursor()\n                try:\n                    cursor.execute(\"BEGIN\")\n                finally:\n                    cursor.close()\n                shared = self._drivers[driver.identity()] = driver\n            return shared\n\n    def rollback(self) -> None:\n        failures = []\n        with self.lock:\n            for identity, driver in self._drivers.items():\n                try:\n                    cursor = driver.pin().cursor()\n                    try:\n                        cursor.execute(\"ROLLBACK\")\n                    finally:\n                        cursor.close()\n                except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - every store is still closed\n                    failures.append(f\"{identity}: {exc}\")\n                finally:\n                    driver.close()\n            self._drivers.clear()\n        if failures:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"acceptance rollback failed: \" + \"; \".join(failures))\n\n\n_harness: _AcceptanceTransaction | None = None\n\n\ndef begin_acceptance_transaction() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Join every store this process opens from now on to one transaction the harness owns.\"\"\"\n    global _harness\n    if _harness is None:\n        _harness = _AcceptanceTransaction()\n\n\ndef end_acceptance_transaction() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Roll back the harness's transaction on every store it joined.\"\"\"\n    global _harness\n    harness, _harness = _harness, None\n    if harness is not None:\n        harness.rollback()\n\n\nclass Database:\n    \"\"\"One store, presented to callers as declared tables with declared methods.\n\n    Callers construct one instance, share it freely, and call methods synchronously. Connection\n    handling is internal and may change without affecting any caller.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, dsn: str, schema: Schema, *, driver: Driver | None = None) -> None:\n        self._rollback_owner = None\n        self._schema = schema\n        driver = driver if driver is not None else open_driver(dsn)\n        self._harness = _harness\n        self._driver = self._harness.join(driver) if self._harness is not None else driver\n        grouped = schema.by_table()\n        for table in schema.tables:\n            setattr(self, table.name, TableAccess(table, grouped.get(table.name, ()), self))\n\n    @property\n    def driver(self) -> Driver:\n        if self._harness is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"driver access is forbidden inside the acceptance transaction\")\n        if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"driver access is forbidden inside a rollback session\")\n        return self._driver\n\n    def close(self) -> None:\n        if self._harness is not None:\n            return  # the acceptance harness owns the shared connection\n        if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"the rollback session owns connection lifetime\")\n        self._driver.close()\n\n    @contextmanager\n    def rollback_session(self):\n        \"\"\"Use this connection for setup, behavior and assertions; always roll back.\n\n        Normal calls remain autocommitted. No schema creation, nested transaction,\n        driver escape, or cross-thread operation is allowed in this scope. Under the acceptance\n        harness the scope is the harness's transaction, rolled back when the criterion ends, so\n        leaving it rolls nothing back.\n        \"\"\"\n        if self._harness is not None:\n            yield self\n            return\n        if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"nested rollback session\")\n        connection = self._driver.connect()\n        cursor = connection.cursor()\n        try:\n            cursor.execute(\"BEGIN\")\n            self._rollback_owner = threading.get_ident()\n            try:\n                yield self\n            finally:\n                try:\n                    cursor.execute(\"ROLLBACK\")\n                except Exception as exc:\n                    raise PersistenceError(f\"acceptance rollback failed: {exc}\") from exc\n                finally:\n                    self._rollback_owner = None\n        finally:\n            cursor.close()\n            self._driver.close()\n\n    def __enter__(self) -> Database:\n        return self\n\n    def __exit__(self, *_: object) -> None:\n        self.close()\n\n    def execute_script(self, sql: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Apply generated DDL. The schema is built once, at the DATABASE build step.\"\"\"\n        if self._rollback_owner is not None or self._harness is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"schema and transaction SQL are forbidden in rollback sessions\")\n        cursor = self._open(\"schema\")\n        try:\n            for statement in statements(self._driver.prepare_schema(sql)):\n                cursor.execute(statement)\n        finally:\n            cursor.close()\n\n    def run(self, operation: Operation, arguments: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Any:\n        \"\"\"Execute one declared operation with bound parameters.\"\"\"\n        unknown = sorted(set(arguments) - set(operation.inputs))\n        if unknown:\n            raise PersistenceError(\n                f\"{operation.identifier} does not accept {', '.join(unknown)}. Declared inputs: \"\n                f\"{', '.join(operation.inputs) or 'none'}.\"\n            )\n        if operation not in self._schema.operations:\n            raise UnknownOperation(f\"{operation.identifier} is not a declared operation\")\n        missing = [name for name in self._match(operation) if name not in arguments]\n        if missing:\n            raise PersistenceError(f\"{operation.identifier} requires {', '.join(missing)}\")\n        if operation.verb == \"delete\" and not arguments:\n            raise PersistenceError(f\"{operation.identifier} requires a delete predicate\")\n        names = [name for name in operation.inputs if name in arguments]\n        values = [arguments[name] for name in names]\n        # The harness's one connection serves the criterion and the application's request\n        # threads alike, so an operation holds it for its whole statement and savepoint.\n        with self._harness.lock if self._harness is not None else nullcontext():\n            scoped = self._rollback_owner is not None or self._harness is not None\n            cursor = self._open(operation.identifier)\n            try:\n                if scoped:\n                    cursor.execute(\"SAVEPOINT drydock_operation\")\n                result = self._dispatch(operation, cursor, names, values)\n                if scoped:\n                    cursor.execute(\"RELEASE SAVEPOINT drydock_operation\")\n                return result\n            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - translated at the boundary on purpose\n                if scoped:\n                    cursor.execute(\"ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT drydock_operation\")\n                    cursor.execute(\"RELEASE SAVEPOINT drydock_operation\")\n                raise PersistenceError(f\"{operation.identifier} failed: {exc}\") from exc\n            finally:\n                cursor.close()\n\n    def _open(self, action: str) -> Any:\n        \"\"\"Return a cursor, translating a refused or failed connection.\"\"\"\n        if self._rollback_owner not in (None, threading.get_ident()):\n            raise PersistenceError(\"rollback session requires its owning thread and connection\")\n        try:\n            return self._driver.connect().cursor()\n        except PersistenceError:\n            raise\n        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - translated at the boundary on purpose\n            raise PersistenceError(f\"{action} could not connect: {exc}\") from exc\n\n    def _dispatch(\n        self,\n        operation: Operation,\n        cursor: Any,\n        names: list[str],\n        values: list[Any],\n    ) -> Any:\n        verb = operation.verb\n        table = operation.table\n        match = self._match(operation)\n        if verb in (\"get\", \"list\"):\n            columns = operation.columns or self._columns(table)\n            statement = self._driver.select(\n                table, columns, names, operation.compare, operation.order\n            )\n            cursor.execute(statement, values)\n            rows = cursor.fetchall() if verb == \"list\" else cursor.fetchmany(1)\n            built = [self._build(operation, columns, row) for row in rows]\n            return built if verb == \"list\" else (built[0] if built else None)\n        if verb == \"create\":\n            key = self._primary_key(table)\n            cursor.execute(self._driver.insert(table, names, key), values)\n            identity = self._driver.inserted_key(cursor)\n            if operation.row is None:\n                return identity\n            # The declared Output row, read back so column defaults are included. A supplied key\n            # wins over the engine's report: SQLite's lastrowid is the rowid, not a text key.\n            if key is None:\n                return self._build(operation, names, values)\n            if key in names:\n                identity = values[names.index(key)]\n            columns = operation.columns or self._columns(table)\n            cursor.execute(self._driver.select(table, columns, [key]), [identity])\n            return self._build(operation, columns, cursor.fetchone())\n        if verb == \"update\":\n            if not match:\n                raise PersistenceError(f\"{operation.identifier} updates {table} without a match\")\n            assigned = [name for name in names if name not in match]\n            if not assigned:\n                raise PersistenceError(f\"{operation.identifier} supplies no column to set\")\n            keys = [values[names.index(name)] for name in match]\n            ordered = [values[names.index(name)] for name in assigned] + keys\n            cursor.execute(self._driver.update(table, assigned, match, operation.compare), ordered)\n            if operation.row is None:\n                return cursor.rowcount\n            if not cursor.rowcount:\n                return None\n            # The declared Output row, read back by its equality match so unassigned columns are\n            # included; a row-returning update matches a unique key by equality.\n            columns = operation.columns or self._columns(table)\n            equal = operation.keys() if operation.match else match\n            cursor.execute(\n                self._driver.select(table, columns, equal, operation.compare),\n                [values[names.index(name)] for name in equal],\n            )\n            return self._build(operation, columns, cursor.fetchone())\n        if verb == \"upsert\":\n            cursor.execute(self._driver.upsert(table, names, match), values)\n            if operation.row is None:\n                return cursor.rowcount\n            columns = operation.columns or self._columns(table)\n            keys = [values[names.index(name)] for name in match]\n            cursor.execute(self._driver.select(table, columns, match), keys)\n            return self._build(operation, columns, cursor.fetchone())\n        if verb == {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01SRfeRXGv49CNdnFMbkFocc","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"Shared input rules: integer-cent amounts, field and date validators, and the projected-balance guard.\n\nEvery command takes its input through these functions so no command repeats or contradicts them.\nValidators and the guard raise ``Rejected`` and never write to the store.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport datetime\nimport re\nfrom collections.abc import Mapping\n\nfrom persistence import Database\n\nfrom cli.errors import Rejected\n\n_AMOUNT = re.compile(r\"(-?)([0-9]+)(?:\\.([0-9]{1,2}))?\")\n_CODE = re.compile(r\"[A-Z0-9]{1,12}\")\n_DATE = re.compile(r\"([0-9]{4})-([0-9]{2})-([0-9]{2})\")\n_FORBIDDEN_TEXT = (\",\", \"\\n\", \"\\r\")\n\n\ndef parse_amount(text: str) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return ``text`` as integer cents. Accepts ``-?DIGITS[.D[D]]`` only; zero is rejected.\"\"\"\n    match = _AMOUNT.fullmatch(text)\n    if match is None:\n        raise Rejected(f\"amount must look like 12.50 or -3: {text!r}\")\n    sign, whole, fraction = match.groups()\n    cents = int(whole) * 100 + int((fraction or \"\").ljust(2, \"0\"))\n    if cents == 0:\n        raise Rejected(\"amount must not be zero\")\n    return -cents if sign else cents\n\n\ndef format_amount(cents: int) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return ``cents`` with exactly two decimals, a leading minus when negative, and no separators.\"\"\"\n    sign = \"-\" if cents < 0 else \"\"\n    magnitude = abs(cents)\n    return f\"{sign}{magnitude // 100}.{magnitude % 100:02d}\"\n\n\ndef validate_code(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return ``text`` if it is 1 to 12 characters from ``A-Z`` and ``0-9``.\"\"\"\n    if _CODE.fullmatch(text) is None:\n        raise Rejected(f\"code must be 1 to 12 characters of A-Z or 0-9: {text!r}\")\n    return text\n\n\ndef validate_text(text: str, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return ``text`` if its length is within bounds and it holds no comma or line break.\"\"\"\n    if not min_len <= len(text) <= max_len:\n        raise Rejected(f\"text must be {min_len} to {max_len} characters: {text!r}\")\n    if any(mark in text for mark in _FORBIDDEN_TEXT):\n        raise Rejected(\"text must not contain a comma or line break\")\n    return text\n\n\ndef validate_name(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return an account name or category description: 1 to 40 characters.\"\"\"\n    return validate_text(text, 1, 40)\n\n\ndef validate_memo(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return a transaction memo: 0 to 60 characters.\"\"\"\n    return validate_text(text, 0, 60)\n\n\ndef validate_date(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return ``text`` if it is a real calendar date written as ``YYYY-MM-DD``.\"\"\"\n    match = _DATE.fullmatch(text)\n    if match is None:\n        raise Rejected(f\"date must look like 2026-04-01: {text!r}\")\n    year, month, day = (int(part) for part in match.groups())\n    try:\n        datetime.date(year, month, day)\n    except ValueError as exc:\n        raise Rejected(f\"not a real calendar date: {text!r}\") from exc\n    return text\n\n\ndef account_balance(db: Database, account: str) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the sum of an account's transaction amounts in cents; zero when it has none.\"\"\"\n    return sum(row.amount for row in db.transactions.list(account=account))\n\n\ndef balance_guard(db: Database, deltas: Mapping[str, int]) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Reject the change set if any account's balance after its delta would go below zero.\n\n    ``deltas`` maps account code to a net change in cents. Nothing is written.\n    \"\"\"\n    for account in sorted(deltas):\n        resulting = account_balance(db, account) + deltas[account]\n        if resulting < 0:\n            raise Rejected(\n                f\"account {account} would be {format_amount(resulting)}; balance may not go negative\"\n            )\n----\ndef test_parse_amount_accepts_one_and_two_decimals_at_the_boundaries():\n    assert parse_amount(\"-0.01\") == -1\n    assert parse_amount(\"-5\") == -500\n\n\ndef test_parse_amount_rejects_non_ascii_digits():\n    assert _rejects(parse_amount, \"١.00\")\n\n\n# format_amount\n\ndef test_format_amount_prints_negative_with_leading_minus():\n    assert format_amount(-1250) == \"-12.50\"\n\n\ndef test_format_amount_prints_zero_with_two_decimals():\n    assert format_amount(0) == \"0.00\"\n\n\ndef test_format_amount_prints_whole_amount_with_two_decimals():\n    assert format_amount(500000) == \"5000.00\"\n\n\ndef test_format_amount_pads_a_single_cent_digit():\n    assert format_amount(5) == \"0.05\"\n\n\ndef test_format_amount_has_no_thousands_separator():\n    assert \",\" not in format_amount(123456789)\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"cents\", [1, -1, 99, 100, -100, 123456, -987654, 500000])\ndef test_format_amount_round_trips_through_parse_amount(cents):\n    assert parse_amount(format_amount(cents)) == cents\n\n\n# validate_code\n\ndef test_validate_code_accepts_twelve_characters():\n    good = \"A\" * 12\n    assert validate_code(good) == good\n\n\ndef {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CgPHDNyyEwTiRGcfTqQp8","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_019AG2J1hcM98zkf8syUFrX5","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/LayersTesting/runs/20261025.160726/build/LayersTesting/cli/views.py","content":"\"\"\"Output shapes, id parsing, and row builders shared by the command modules.\n\nCommands build their rows here so every table prints the same way. Nothing in this module reads\nor writes the store except ``next_txn_id``, which only reads.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nfrom typing import NamedTuple\n\nfrom persistence import Database\n\nfrom cli.core import format_amount\nfrom cli.errors import Rejected, UsageError\n\nACCOUNT_COLUMNS = [\"account\", \"name\"]\nCATEGORY_COLUMNS = [\"category\", \"description\"]\nTXN_COLUMNS = [\"txn_id\", \"date\", \"account\", \"category\", \"amount\", \"memo\"]\nACCOUNT_HEADER = [\"account\", \"name\", \"transactions\", \"balance\"]\nTXN_HEADER = TXN_COLUMNS\nLOADED_HEADER = [\"table\", \"loaded\"]\nTRANSFER_CATEGORY = \"TRANSFER\"\n\n#: The largest id the transactions table holds (INTEGER on PostgreSQL). A file id must fit it.\nTXN_ID_MAX = 2**31 - 1\n\n_ID_TEXT = re.compile(r\"-?[0-9]+\")\n_LOADED_ID = re.compile(r\"[0-9]+\")\n\n\nclass Txn(NamedTuple):\n    \"\"\"One transaction ready to store, in the column order of the transactions table.\"\"\"\n\n    txn_id: int\n    date: str\n    account: str\n    category: str\n    amount: int\n    memo: str\n\n\ndef parse_txn_id(text: str) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return a transaction id argument. Anything but a base-10 integer is a usage error.\"\"\"\n    if _ID_TEXT.fullmatch(text) is None:\n        raise UsageError(f\"transaction id must be an integer: {text!r}\")\n    return int(text)\n\n\ndef load_txn_id(text: str) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return a transaction id read from a file: a positive integer that fits the column.\"\"\"\n    if _LOADED_ID.fullmatch(text) is None or not 1 <= int(text) <= TXN_ID_MAX:\n        raise Rejected(f\"txn_id must be a positive integer up to {TXN_ID_MAX}: {text!r}\")\n    return int(text)\n\n\ndef next_txn_id(db: Database) -> int:\n Nothing in this module reads\nor writes the store except ``next_txn_id``, which only reads.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nfrom typing import NamedTuple\n\nfrom persistence import Database\n\nfrom cli.core import format_amount\nfrom cli.errors import Rejected, UsageError\n\nACCOUNT_COLUMNS = [\"account\", \"name\"]\nCATEGORY_COLUMNS = [\"category\", \"description\"]\nTXN_COLUMNS = [\"txn_id\", \"date\", \"account\", \"category\", \"amount\", \"memo\"]\nACCOUNT_HEADER = [\"account\", \"name\", \"transactions\", \"balance\"]\nTXN_HEADER = TXN_COLUMNS\nLOADED_HEADER = [\"table\", \"loaded\"]\nTRANSFER_CATEGORY = \"TRANSFER\"\n\n#: The largest id the transactions table holds (INTEGER on PostgreSQL). {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CgPHHxiMBJMuwvezcULtZ","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_011ucG2vBLTNqysfwEqqzKP3","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cat > cli/commands/load.py <<'EOF'\n\"\"\"``ledger load``: read one CSV file whole, validate every row, then store every row or none.\n\nEvery check runs before the first write. The persistence package offers no multi-statement\ntransaction to application code, so the all-or-nothing guarantee rests on that ordering.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport csv\nfrom typing import NamedTuple\n\nfrom cli.context import open_store\nfrom cli.core import (\n    balance_guard,\n    parse_amount,\n    validate_code,\n    validate_date,\n    validate_memo,\n    validate_name,\n)\nfrom cli.errors import OperationalError, Rejected\nfrom cli.registry import register\nfrom cli.views import (\n    ACCOUNT_COLUMNS,\n    CATEGORY_COLUMNS,\n    LOADED_HEADER,\n    TXN_COLUMNS,\n    Txn,\n    load_txn_id,\n)\n\n\ndef load_accounts(args: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    (path,) = args\n    body = _read(path, ACCOUNT_COLUMNS)\n    for code, name in body:\n        validate_code(code)\n        validate_name(name)\n    with open_store() as db:\n        stored = {account.account for account in db.accounts.list()}\n        _reject_repeats([code for code, _ in body], stored)\n        for code, name in body:\n            db.accounts.create(account=code, name=name)\n    return [LOADED_HEADER, [\"accounts\", str(len(body))]]\n\n\ndef load_categories(args: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    (path,) = args\n    body = _read(path, CATEGORY_COLUMNS)\n    for code, description in body:\n        validate_code(code)\n        validate_name(description)\n    with open_store() as db:\n        stored = {category.category for category in db.categories.list()}\n        _reject_repeats([code for code, _ in body], stored)\n        for code, description in body:\n            db.categories.create(category=code, description=description)\n    return [LOADED_HEADER, [\"categories\", str(len(body))]]\n\n\ndef load_transactions(args: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    (path,) = args\n    txns = [_parse_txn(row) for row in _read(path, TXN_COLUMNS)]\n    with open_store() as db:\n        accounts = {account.account for account in db.accounts.list()}\n        categories = {category.category for category in db.categories.list()}\n        for txn in txns:\n            if txn.account not in accounts:\n                raise Rejected(f\"unknown account {txn.account}\")\n            if txn.category not in categories:\n                raise Rejected(f\"unknown category {txn.category}\")\n        stored = {txn.txn_id for txn in db.transactions.list()}\n        _reject_repeats([txn.txn_id for txn in txns], stored)\n        deltas: dict[str, int] = {}\n        for txn in txns:\n            deltas[txn.account] = deltas.get(txn.account, 0) + txn.amount\n        balance_guard(db, deltas)\n        for txn in txns:\n            db.transactions.create(**txn._asdict())\n    return [LOADED_HEADER, [\"transactions\", str(len(txns))]]\n\n\nclass _Row(NamedTuple):\n    \"\"\"Placeholder type so the row parser's return is named in one place.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef _parse_txn(row: list[str]) -> Txn:\n    txn_id, day, account, category, amount, memo = row\n    return Txn(\n        txn_id=load_txn_id(txn_id),\n        date=validate_date(day),\n        account=validate_code(account),\n        category=validate_code(category),\n        amount=parse_amount(amount),\n        memo=validate_memo(memo),\n    )\n\n\ndef _read(path: str, columns: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Return the body rows of ``path`` once its header and field counts check out.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        with open(path, newline=\"\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n            rows = list(csv.reader(handle))\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, csv.Error) as exc:\n        raise OperationalError(f\"cannot read {path}: {exc}\") from exc\n    if not rows or rows[0] != columns:\n        raise Rejected(f\"header must be {','.join(columns)}\")\n    body = rows[1:]\n    for number, row in enumerate(body, start=2):\n        if len(row) != len(columns):\n            raise Rejected(f\"line {number} must have {len(columns)} fields\")\n    return body\n\n\ndef _reject_repeats(keys: list, stored: set) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Refuse a key that repeats inside the file or is already stored.\"\"\"\n    seen: set = set()\n    for key in keys:\n        if key in seen:\n            raise Rejected(f\"{key} repeats in the file\")\n        if key in stored:\n            raise Rejected(f\"{key} is already stored\")\n        seen.add(key)\n\n\nregister((\"load\", \"accounts\"), load_accounts, (1, 1))\nregister((\"load\", \"categories\"), load_categories, (1, 1))\nregister((\"load\", \"transactions\"), load_transactions, (1, 1))\nEOF\necho ok","description":"Write load command row, then store every row or none.\n\nEvery check runs before the first write. The persistence package offers no multi-statement\ntransaction to application code, so the all-or-nothing guarantee rests on that ordering.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport csv\nfrom typing import NamedTuple\n\nfrom cli.context import open_store\nfrom cli.core import (\n    balance_guard,\n    parse_amount,\n    validate_code,\n    validate_date,\n    validate_memo,\n    validate_name,\n)\nfrom cli.errors import OperationalError, Rejected\nfrom cli.registry import register\nfrom cli.views import (\n    ACCOUNT_COLUMNS,\n    CATEGORY_COLUMNS,\n    LOADED_HEADER,\n    TXN_COLUMNS,\n    Txn,\n    load_txn_id,\n)\n\n\ndef load_accounts(args: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    (path,) = args\n    body = _read(path, ACCOUNT_COLUMNS)\n    for code, name in body:\n        validate_code(code)\n        validate_name(name)\n    with open_store() as db:\n        stored = {account.account for account in db.accounts.list()}\n        _reject_repeats([code for code, _ in body], stored)\n        for code, name in body:\n            db.accounts.create(account=code, name=name)\n    return [LOADED_HEADER, [\"accounts\", str(len(body))]]\n\n\ndef load_categories(args: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    (path,) = args\n    body = _read(path, CATEGORY_COLUMNS)\n    for code, description in body:\n        validate_code(code)\n        validate_name(description)\n    with open_store() as db:\n        stored = {category.category for category in db.categories.list()}\n        _reject_repeats([code for code, _ in body], stored)\n        for code, description in body:\n            db.categories.create(category=code, description=description)\n    return [LOADED_HEADER, [\"categories\", str(len(body))]]\n\n\ndef load_transactions(args: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    (path,) = args\n    txns = [_parse_txn(row) for row in _read(path, TXN_COLUMNS)]\n    with open_store() as db:\n        accounts = {account.account for account in db.accounts.list()}\n        categories = {category.category for category in db.categories.list()}\n        for txn in txns:\n            if txn.account not in accounts:\n                raise Rejected(f\"unknown account {txn.account}\")\n            if txn.category not in categories:\n                raise Rejected(f\"unknown category {txn.category}\")\n        stored = {txn.txn_id for txn in db.transactions.list()}\n        _reject_repeats([txn.txn_id for txn in txns], stored)\n        deltas: dict[str, int] = {}\n        for txn in txns:\n            deltas[txn.account] = deltas.get(txn.account, 0) + txn.amount\n        balance_guard(db, deltas)\n        for txn in txns:\n            db.transactions.create(**txn._asdict())\n    return [LOADED_HEADER, [\"transactions\", str(len(txns))]]\n\n\nclass _Row(NamedTuple):\n    \"\"\"Placeholder type so the row parser's return is named in one place.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef _parse_txn(row: list[str]) -> Txn:\n    txn_id, day, account, category, amount, memo = row\n    return Txn(\n        txn_id=load_txn_id(txn_id),\n        date=validate_date(day),\n        account=validate_code(account),\n        category=validate_code(category),\n        amount=parse_amount(amount),\n        memo=validate_memo(memo),\n    )\n\n\ndef _read(path: str, columns: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Return the body rows of ``path`` once its header and field counts check out.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        with open(path, newline=\"\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n            rows = list(csv.reader(handle))\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, csv.Error) as exc:\n        raise OperationalError(f\"cannot read {path}: {exc}\") from exc\n    if not rows or rows[0] != columns:\n        raise Rejected(f\"header must be {','.join(columns)}\")\n    body = rows[1:]\n    for number, row in enumerate(body, start=2):\n        if len(row) != len(columns):\n            raise Rejected(f\"line {number} must have {len(columns)} fields\")\n    return body\n\n\ndef _reject_repeats(keys: list, stored: set) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Refuse a key that repeats inside the file or is already stored.\"\"\"\n    seen: set = set()\n    for key in keys:\n        if key in seen:\n            raise Rejected(f\"{key} repeats in the file\")\n        if key in stored:\n            raise Rejected(f\"{key} is already stored\")\n        seen.add(key)\n\n\nregister((\"load\", \"accounts\"), load_accounts, (1, 1))\nregister((\"load\", \"categories\"), load_categories, (1, 1))\nregister((\"load\", \"transactions\"), load_transactions, (1, 1))\nEOF\necho ok","description":"Write load command module"}},"wire_ingest_context":{"toolu_011ucG2vBLTNqysfwEqqzKP3":{"cwd":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/LayersTesting/runs/20261025.160726/build/LayersTesting"}}}

   validate_name(name)\n    with open_store() as db:\n        stored = {account.account for account in db.accounts.list()}\n        _reject_repeats([code for code, _ in body], stored)\n        for code, name in body:\n            db.accounts.create(account=code, name=name)\n    return [LOADED_HEADER, [\"accounts\", str(len(body))]]\n\n\ndef load_categories(args: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    (path,) = args\n    body = _read(path, CATEGORY_COLUMNS)\n    for code, description in body:\n        validate_code(code)\n        validate_name(description)\n    with open_store() as db:\n        stored = {category.category for category in db.categories.list()}\n        _reject_repeats([code for code, _ in body], stored)\n        for code, description in body:\n            db.categories.create(category=code, description=description)\n    return [LOADED_HEADER, [\"categories\", str(len(body))]]\n\n\ndef load_transactions(args: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    (path,) = args\n    txns = [_parse_txn(row) for row in _read(path, TXN_COLUMNS)]\n    with open_store() as db:\n        accounts = {account.account for account in db.accounts.list()}\n        categories = {category.category for category in db.categories.list()}\n        for txn in txns:\n            if txn.account not in accounts:\n                raise Rejected(f\"unknown account {txn.account}\")\n            if txn.category not in categories:\n                raise Rejected(f\"unknown category {txn.category}\")\n        stored = {txn.txn_id for txn in db.transactions.list()}\n        _reject_repeats([txn.txn_id for txn in txns], stored)\n        deltas: dict[str, int] = {}\n        for txn in txns:\n            deltas[txn.account] = deltas.get(txn.account, 0) + txn.amount\n        balance_guard(db, deltas)\n        for txn in txns:\n            db.transactions.create(**txn._asdict())\n    return [LOADED_HEADER, [\"transactions\", str(len(txns))]]\n\n\nclass _Row(NamedTuple):\n       txn_id=load_txn_id(txn_id),\n        date=validate_date(day),\n        account=validate_code(account),\n        category=validate_code(category),\n        amount=parse_amount(amount),\n        memo=validate_memo(memo),\n    )\n\n\ndef _read(path: str, columns: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Return the body rows of ``path`` once its header and field counts check out.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        with open(path, newline=\"\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n            rows = list(csv.reader(handle))\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, csv.Error) as exc:\n        raise row in enumerate(body, start=2):\n        if len(row) != len(columns):\n            raise Rejected(f\"line {number} must have {len(columns)} fields\")\n    return body\n\n\ndef _reject_repeats(keys: Rejected(f\"{key} repeats in the file\")\n        if key in stored:\n            raise Rejected(f\"{key} is already stored\")\n        seen.add(key)\n\n\nregister((\"load\", \"accounts\"), cli.context import open_store\nfrom cli.core import (\n    balance_guard,\n    parse_amount,\n    validate_code,\n    validate_date,\n    validate_memo,\n    validate_name,\n)\nfrom cli.errors import load_txn_id,\n)\n\n\ndef load_accounts(args: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    (path,) = args\n    body = _read(path, ACCOUNT_COLUMNS)\n    for code, name in body:\n        validate_code(code)\n        validate_name(name)\n    with open_store() as db:\n        stored = {account.account for account in db.accounts.list()}\n        _reject_repeats([code for code, _ in body], stored)\n        for code, name in body:\n            db.accounts.create(account=code, name=name)\n    return [LOADED_HEADER, [\"accounts\", str(len(body))]]\n\n\ndef load_categories(args: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    (path,) = args\n    body = _read(path, CATEGORY_COLUMNS)\n    for code, description in body:\n        validate_code(code)\n        validate_name(description)\n    with open_store() as db:\n        stored = {category.category for category in db.categories.list()}\n        _reject_repeats([code for code, _ in body], stored)\n        for code, description in body:\n            db.categories.create(category=code, description=description)\n    return [LOADED_HEADER, [\"categories\", str(len(body))]]\n\n\ndef load_transactions(args: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    (path,) = args\n    txns = [_parse_txn(row) for row in _read(path, TXN_COLUMNS)]\n    with open_store() as db:\n        accounts = {account.account for account in db.accounts.list()}\n        categories = {category.category for category in db.categories.list()}\n        for txn in txns:\n            if txn.account not in accounts:\n                raise Rejected(f\"unknown account {txn.account}\")\n            if txn.category not in categories:\n                raise Rejected(f\"unknown category {txn.category}\")\n        stored = {txn.txn_id for txn in db.transactions.list()}\n        _reject_repeats([txn.txn_id for txn in txns], stored)\n        deltas: dict[str, int] = {}\n        for txn in txns:\n            deltas[txn.account] = deltas.get(txn.account, 0) + txn.amount\n        balance_guard(db, deltas)\n        for txn in txns:\n            db.transactions.create(**txn._asdict())\n    return [LOADED_HEADER, [\"transactions\", str(len(txns))]]\n\n\ndef _parse_txn(row: list[str]) -> Txn:\n    txn_id, day, account, category, amount, memo = row\n    return Txn(\n        txn_id=load_txn_id(txn_id),\n        date=validate_date(day),\n        account=validate_code(account),\n        category=validate_code(category),\n        amount=parse_amount(amount),\n        memo=validate_memo(memo),\n    )\n\n\ndef _read(path: str, columns: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Return the body rows of ``path`` once its header and field counts check out.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        with open(path, newline=\"\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n            rows = list(csv.reader(handle))\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, csv.Error) as exc:\n        raise OperationalError(f\"cannot read {path}: {exc}\") from exc\n    if not rows or rows[0] != columns:\n        raise Rejected(f\"header must be {','.join(columns)}\")\n    body = rows[1:]\n    for number, row in enumerate(body, start=2):\n        if len(row) != len(columns):\n            raise Rejected(f\"line {number} must have {len(columns)} fields\")\n    return body\n\n\ndef _reject_repeats(keys: list, stored: set) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Refuse a key that repeats inside the file or is already stored.\"\"\"\n    seen: set = set()\n    for key in keys:\n        if key in seen:\n            raise Rejected(f\"{key} repeats in the file\")\n        if key in stored:\n            raise Rejected(f\"{key} is already stored\")\n        seen.add(key)\n\n\nregister((\"load\", \"accounts\"), load_accounts, (1, 1))\nregister((\"load\", \"categories\"), load_categories, (1,
